svg.title: How the harness is built, and how it holds itself
svg.desc: Two panels. Part A, generation: three sources - the codebase in brownfield, the specs in greenfield, and the human at intake - each derive specific artifacts. The codebase analysis produces the Inventory Report, whose module map gives one dev agent per module, whose conventions give the three project-specific rules, whose risky operations give the deny list and the hooks, whose glob sets give the path frontmatter that makes rules lazy-load, and whose detected stack decides which skills are even worth offering. The specs give FR clusters and the flags: db alone fields the data-modeler, while db_engineer and db_seeder add their seats only when that work is real; ui fields the frontend-ui-dev seat; ai adds the prompt-injection clauses. The human answers only what code cannot decide, including what to test and which methodology to run. All three converge into vars.json, which carries the full flag set - ui, db, db_engineer, db_seeder, ai, audit, tdd, ddd, light, unit, e2e, tests, deploy_ask, long, solo_review, terse, and exactly one of windows or posix - and drives scaffold.py, a deterministic funnel that copies real files, substitutes variables, resolves flag blocks, never overwrites, and exits non-zero on an unresolved variable. It emits 16 seat files of which 10 are flag-gated, 16 rules, 22 commands, 9 hooks with settings.json, the python scripts, and the task board. The model authors only what cannot be templated. Part B, mutual constraint: a green enforcement band of hooks, deny list, maxTurns and the harness-toggle ledger encloses a closed ring in which the orchestrator dispatches but cannot build, spec-guardian locks the contract, the dev agents write code but only inside their module paths, the reviewers - two seats, or one merged reviewer under solo_review - gate them with no Edit and no Write, and the task board holds the orchestrator to account. Governance decides which model may touch a class of data before dispatch, and the rules are drawn soft and dashed because they are advisory.
svg.text: How the harness is built, and how it holds itself
Part A - generation: nothing is invented. Part B - constraint: nothing is trusted.
PART A GENERATION - where every generated file comes from
Every generated thing traces to the codebase, to the specs, or to an answer you gave.
codebase analysis, read-only, produces the Inventory Report you confirm
-> one dev agent per module, scoped to real paths
-> the settings.json deny list, and which hooks
-> the paths: frontmatter, so rules lazy-load
-> which skills are even worth offering you
-> one dev agent per feature domain
db_seeder add their seats when that work is real
answers only what the code cannot decide:
data classification, gated actions, licences, commit
identity, dev OS (flag windows or posix), and two
choices nobody should default: what to test, and how.
audit, tdd, ddd, light, unit, e2e,
and exactly one of windows | posix
the one funnel every file passes
The model authors only what cannot be templated: the routing table, each dev agent's scope,
and the 3 project-specific rules. Everything else is a file copy.
PART B MUTUAL CONSTRAINT - each one is held by another
Not a hierarchy. A closed loop, inside a band none of them can open.
HARD - shell scripts and glob rules. No model gets a vote, not even the orchestrator.
what no agent can even see
OFF IS ALSO ON THE RECORD - /harness-toggle + .claude/disabled.json
A control is disabled, never deleted. The HARD tier needs a phrase the user types. Agents: refused entirely.
with NO Edit, NO Write - a
reviewer that edits is a dev.
No agent is trusted, including the one doing the routing. Each is bounded by something it does not control.
And the harness itself is scored: harness-view assess grades it against the same quality gate, with no model in the loop.
